name: 209. Custom OpenAI-compatible provider mints its bearer from oauth_key_config (custom provider oauth)
description:
Pins the oauth_key_config wire contract for custom providers on the openai base. A key may carry no value and instead an OAuth2 client_credentials (or RFC 7523 jwt_bearer) block; OpenAIProvider resolves it at method entry through core/providers/utils/tokencache (ResolveBearer), the same path Databricks OAuth M2M uses, and the management API stores the block with its secrets encrypted and returns it redacted.

Each case stands up a run-scoped custom provider through the management API and deletes it afterwards, sweeping leftovers older than ten minutes. The token endpoint is deliberately unreachable (https://127.0.0.1:9), so the inference case pins the shape of the failure rather than a live IdP: the request must fail at token minting with the token endpoint named and no secret echoed, never with the upstream's 401 that a static-bearer path would produce.

Red before the change: POST /keys without a value is refused (Key value must not be empty), so the OAuth key never exists and the chat case has nothing to mint from. Green after: the key saves, round-trips redacted, and the chat request fails at the mint. The refusal cases pin that allowing a valueless OAuth key did not loosen the empty-key, half-block, token_url, auth_style or signing_algorithm checks. The body-placement case pins that auth_style and audience stay readable while client_id, client_secret and every extra_params value come back masked, and that an update which sends those masks back resolves them to the stored values instead of clearing them. The jwt_bearer cases pin the RFC 7523 grant on the same path: the PEM is stored masked and never echoed, the claims round-trip readable, the chat request fails at the exchange (the assertion signed, the endpoint unreachable), and a literal private_key that is not an RSA or EC PEM is refused at save naming the field, so it never reaches a mint. Refusal rows carry [EXPECT-400] and mint rows [EXPECT-502] (the unreachable token endpoint is a bad gateway), which the collection-level status test must expect.

Run with FEATURE="custom provider oauth".
